title: NURBS Surface Editor
prompt:
Implement an interactive NURBS (or a reasonable approximation using a B-spline/NURBS surface) editor with Three.js.

[Three.js Import Method (Must Be Followed Strictly)]
Use the following import map in <head>, and import via ES Modules in <script type="module">:
<script type="importmap">
{ "imports": {
    "three": "https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/three@0.170.0/build/three.module.js",
    "three/addons/": "https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/three@0.170.0/examples/jsm/"
} }
</script>
<script type="module">
import * as THREE from 'three';
import { OrbitControls } from 'three/addons/controls/OrbitControls.js';
</script>

[Control Grid]
(1) Use a fixed 5×5 control-point grid (25 points), initially arranged on a plane or with slight undulations.
(2) Move control points by mouse dragging (using a Raycaster to hit control-point spheres or handles), and update the surface Mesh in real time.
(3) id="degree": a range input or select element for adjusting the degree/order between 2–5 (a uniform knot vector may be used).
(4) id="showPolygon": a checkbox that toggles the display of the control polygon (polylines/points).

[Surface]
(5) Generate a BufferGeometry using a sufficiently dense parameter-sampling grid (for example, 64×64, or adjusted according to performance), with correct normals.

[State Exposure (Required)]
window.__3D_STATE__ = {
  controlPointCount: number,
  degree: number,
  surfaceVertexCount: number,
  showPolygon: boolean
}

controlPointCount must always be 25; degree must be between 2–5; surfaceVertexCount > 1000.

Output a single HTML file that can run by being opened directly in a browser.
